original_question: If mu is a nonnegative continuous even convex function on [-1,1], must the snake polynomials associated with mu have a nonnegative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting Geno Nikolov’s unnumbered “Conjecture (G.N.)” in the section “Snake polynomials with positive Chebyshev expansions,” not the broader preceding open problem. In paper-faithful form: if μ is a continuous even convex majorant on [-1,1], then the snake polynomials associated with μ should have non-negative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right hypotheses on μ (nonnegative/majorant, continuous, even, convex on [-1,1]), the right object (snake polynomials associated with μ), and the right conclusion (non-negative expansion in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind). It is therefore very close to the actual conjecture stated in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
missing_details: The paper works degree-by-degree: one should quantify over the n-th snake polynomial (for each degree n for which it is defined), not over an unspecified single snake polynomial. The plural wording in the conjecture reflects this degree-dependent family. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The ambient space should be stated: P_n is the space of real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n, and the paper explicitly says one may assume real coefficients. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The existence clause is implicit in your draft: the section first assumes μ is a majorant and that there exists a degree-n polynomial under μ; only then is the associated snake polynomial defined. So a stand-alone version should say “for every n for which the associated n-th snake polynomial exists/ is defined.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The definition of the snake polynomial should be made explicit: it is unique up to orientation, has degree n, satisfies |ω_{μ,n}(x)| ≤ μ(x) on [-1,1], and has n+1 alternation points τ_0<⋯<τ_n with ω_{μ,n}(τ_i)=(-1)^i μ(τ_i). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The phrase “non-negative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind” should be spelled out as a Chebyshev-T expansion ω_{μ,n}(x)=∑_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x) with all coefficients a_j ≥ 0. That is the standard explicit meaning of “positive/non-negative Chebyshev expansion” in the Nikolov–Shadrin literature cited around this problem. ([damtp.cam.ac.uk](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/na/people/Alexei/papers/mds6_00.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should remain the narrow conjecture for continuous even convex majorants, rather than the broader neighboring open problem of characterizing all majorants whose snake polynomials have non-negative or sign-alternating Chebyshev expansions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

No additional structures such as homogeneity, nilpotency, operator conditions, or asymptotic quantifiers occur here; the missing precision is instead about degree, coefficient field, existence, alternation, and the exact meaning of Chebyshev-positivity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
refined_question: For each n for which it is defined, let P_n denote the real polynomials of degree at most n, and let ω_{μ,n}∈P_n be the n-th snake polynomial associated with a majorant μ:[-1,1]→[0,∞), meaning the unique (up to orientation) degree-n polynomial satisfying |ω_{μ,n}(x)|≤μ(x) on [-1,1] and possessing n+1 alternation points -1≤τ_0<⋯<τ_n≤1 with ω_{μ,n}(τ_i)=(-1)^i μ(τ_i). If μ is continuous, even, and convex on [-1,1], must every such ω_{μ,n} admit a Chebyshev expansion of the first kind ω_{μ,n}(x)=∑_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x) with a_j≥0 for all j? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
justification: The closest official target is the unnumbered “Conjecture (G.N.)” in the Nikolov section. The draft is already close because it uses the same hypothesis class (continuous even convex μ on [-1,1]) and the same conclusion (non-negative Chebyshev-T expansion). What needed sharpening was the surrounding notation and scope supplied by the nearby context: the section first defines P_n, majorants, and the snake polynomial via maximal oscillation/alternation, and then explains that this positivity question matters because earlier work showed the Markov/Duffin–Schaeffer extremal equalities when a snake polynomial has non-negative or sign-alternating Chebyshev expansion. I therefore kept the question narrow and simply made the degree quantifier, existence clause, alternation definition, real coefficient field, and the coefficientwise meaning of “non-negative expansion” explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
